meta.description: Comprehensive accuracy improvement experiments for cyclone track forecasting
meta.protocol: Validation selects, test verifies. No test-set tuning.

champion.model: LightGBM displacement (26 features, per-horizon lat/lon regressors)

E06_blend.verdict: IMPROVED on validation; on test beats MV by 6-10% but trails LightGBM by ~2%

E07_boosting_compare.findings: CatBoost slightly better at 6h (35.07 vs 35.13) and 12h (71.72 vs 73.07). XGBoost best at 24h (153.28 vs 159.82). All beat movement-vector baseline.

E08_lgbm_search.findings: Shallower trees (depth=3) with higher learning rate slightly better on val but similar on test. Baseline config was already near-optimal.

E09_feature_ablation.description: Remove each feature group, measure impact
E09_feature_ablation.findings: Current state (state0) and recent velocity are critical. Turn rate and 24h trend are slightly harmful on test, suggesting regularization benefit.

strong_storms.note: Strong storms are easiest to track

E10_error_analysis.findings: Weak storms (low wind) are hardest to track (2x error at 24h). Fast-moving storms degrade more at 24h. Median is 15-18% below mean, indicating right-skewed error distribution.

summary.overall_verdict: LightGBM displacement model is well-tuned. The baseline config outperforms or matches tuned alternatives.
summary.best_ensemble: E06 Blend with LightGBM (validation IMPROVED, test marginal)
summary.key_insight: Feature engineering is more impactful than algorithm choice. State0+velocity features account for most predictive power.
summary.remaining_gap: Weak storms remain challenging. Environmental wind features (sst, env_speed) add negligible value with current feature set.
